classes.name: Testosterone replacement
classes.description: Testosterone gel/solution (AndroGel, Testim, Fortesta, Vogelxo, generic 1%/1.62%), injections (cypionate, enanthate, Xyosted, Aveed undecanoate), patch (Androderm), oral undecanoate (Jatenzo, Tlando, Kyzatrex), nasal (Natesto), pellets (Testopel).
classes.plainDescription: Testosterone replacement for low testosterone, as a gel, shot or pill.

preferredAgent.sig: 50-400 mg IM every 2 to 4 weeks, adjusted to keep morning testosterone in the normal range (label).
preferredAgent.plainSig: A shot every 2 to 4 weeks; your prescriber sets the dose from blood tests.

records.preferredRestriction: PA required (page 66); PA criteria are not printed on the PDL
records.verificationNote: Every testosterone product on PDL page 66 carries PA, so the pick is the lowest-barrier standard injection (generic 'testosterone injection', P). The cypionate salt is inferred from the common generic product; the PDL does not name the ester. Aveed (undecanoate injection), Testopel (pellets) and Androderm (patch) are not on the PDL; they are provider-administered or not listed, so absence is not an exclusion. Oral methyltestosterone (Methitest) was not picked despite its P status. [Sonnet check 2026-11-02: PDL p66 prints 'testosterone injection generic' P PA with no ester named; cypionate inferred (Depo-Testosterone P PA on the same page is the cypionate brand; Delatestryl P PA is enanthate). Pick stays the generic injection, partial. Moved Depo-Testosterone, gel pump 1.62% and Methitest from alternatives to paRequired because each carries PA.]

preferredAgent.sig: Apply 50 mg (5 g of 1% gel) once daily in the morning to shoulders and upper arms; adjust by serum testosterone, max 100 mg/day (label).

records.verificationNote: Tier 3 and PA for testosterone cypionate 200 mg/mL read by x-coordinate on page 67. The guide prints no PA criteria, so the reason is the PA flag alone. Every other testosterone product in the guide needs PA, so cypionate is the lowest-barrier pick. Partial because injections may be self-administered under Part D or given in a clinic under Part B; the cost path is unconfirmed. Jatenzo, Tlando, Kyzatrex, Xyosted, Aveed, Androderm, Natesto, Testopel and methyltestosterone do not appear in the guide. [Sonnet check 2026-10-27: Re-confirmed against Humana formulary 26402, v17 (updated 10/01/2026), sources/humana-premier-rx-pdp-newtopics-2026-10.pdf (tier, PA, ST, QL read by x-coordinate; the v16 copy used in the first pass is superseded). All testosterone rows (cypionate, enanthate, 1.62% gel packet and pump) are on page 67. Cypionate is Tier 3 with PA and no BvsD flag; enanthate is Tier 3, PA, QL 25 per 90 days; the 1.62% gels are Tier 4 with PA. Cypionate stays the pick: it is the standard generic injectable and carries the same PA as every other listed product, unlike oral methyltestosterone, which is not listed. Part B applies only to clinic-administered injections, so the cost path stays unconfirmed (partial).] [Reused: same national Humana Premier Rx PDP formulary (exported 2026-11-02)]
